 RFA-3949-1998 (O&M) alongwith other connected cases --2-- First Appeals are being decided as all have arisen out of the same award.

1.2 For convenience, the facts are being taken from RFA-3949- 1998 (O&M).
2.

By way of present appeals, challenge has been laid to an Award dated 23.04.1998 passed by the learned Additional District Judge,
Kurukshetra (for short, "Reference Court"), whereby, reference petition(s)
preferred at the instance of appellants-landowners invoking Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for brevity, "1894 Act"), were partly allowed.

3. Brief facts of the case are that some land owned by the appellants-landowners, situated in the revenue estate of Village Jhinwarheri,
Tehsil Thanser, District Kurukshetra was sought to be acquired vide notification dated 13.05.1993 published on 01.06.1993, under Section 4 of the 1894 Act and the notification dated 07.02.1994 published on 01.03.1994,
issued under Section 6 thereof, for the public purpose, namely, construction of road from Jhansa to Jhinwarheri.
The Land Acquisition Collector vide its Award, assessed the market value of the acquired land at the rate of Rs.1,50,000/- per acre.
4. Aggrieved of the same, the appellants-landowners invoked separate reference petition(s) under Section 18 of the 1894 Act, seeking enhancement of compensation.

Upon consideration of the material available on record, the Reference Court vide its Award dated 23.04.1998, enhanced the market value to Rs.1,90,000/- per acre besides granting all other Smt.Dayalo And Ors vs State Of Haryana And Anr on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145350377/
1 statutory benefits.

5. Feeling dissatisfied with the aforesaid Award passed by the ld.
Reference Court

, the landowners as well as State of Haryana preferred the  2 of 5  ::: Downloaded on - 08-11-2025 02:56:36 :::
 RFA-3949-1998 (O&M) alongwith other connected cases --3-- aforementioned appeals.
6. Learned Counsel for the appellants-landowners submits that the ld. Reference Court though rightly placed reliance upon the sale instance Ex.P-2 dated 01.06.1993, however, went wrong while applying the development cut @ 25% upon its sale price.

He contends that the purpose of acquisition in the case in hand was for laying down of road from Village Jhansa to Jhinwarheri and therefore, the respondents were not to suffer any loss of land or even incur cost towards providing of additional infrastructure.

Learned counsel emphasizes that keeping in view the purpose of acquisition and the parcel of land measuring 3 kanals 3 marlas been sold @ Rs.1,00,000/- as per sale instance Ex.P-2, no development cut was required to be imposed and thus, prays for enhancement of compensation.

7. On the other hand, learned State counsel submits that the sale instance Ex.P-2 dated 01.06.1993 was not a bonafide or genuine transaction and thus, could not have been relied upon by the ld.
Reference Court for the purpose of making assessment of compensation.
He points out that the sale instance Ex.P-2 dated 01.06.1993 was executed on the day of publication of the notification under Section 4 of the 1894 Act in the present case.

He thus, submits that the impugned Award passed by the ld. Reference Court was liable to be set aside as no reliable evidence was available on record for the purpose of making re-assessment of compensation.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the paper book.
I find substance in the submissions made on behalf of the appellants-landowners.

9. A perusal of record shows that vide sale instance Ex.P2 dated 3 of 5 RFA-3949-1998 (O&M)
alongwith other connected cases --4-- 01.06.1993, 3 kanals 3 marlas of land was sold for Rs. 1 lakh and the price per acre was Rs.2,53,968/-.

The sale instance Ex. P2 even pertained to the same revenue estate of Village,
Jhinwarheri.

The argument raised on behalf of the respondent-State to the effect that the sale Smt.Dayalo And Ors vs State Of Haryana And Anr on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145350377/
2 instance Ex.P-2 was not bonafide or genuine transaction as it was executed on the same day of publication of notification under Section 4 of the 1894 Act, pertaining to the present acquisition, has no legs to stand.

sentences.text: No evidence from the records has been pointed out to substantiate the aforementioned plea.

In such circumstances, in the absence of any material on record to doubt the genuineness of the sale instance Ex.P2, the same was rightly taken into account as an exemplar being a bonafide sale transaction.

10. Further, as rightly pointed out by the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellants-landowners, the purpose of acquisition in the case in hand being for laying down of road from village Jhansa to Jhinwarheri, the issue about imposition of development cut needs to be re examined.

Considering the fact that the sale instance Ex. P2 pertains to a relatively large area measuring 3 kanals 3 marlas and the respondents neither suffered any loss of land, nor any extra costs for providing any kind of infrastructural development of civic amenities like park, green belt,
community building etc; rather than applying development cut @ 25%, the same should have been applied @ 10%, especially, when the area under acquisition which formed part of the revenue estate of village Jhinwarheri was merely 0.79 acres.

11. Accordingly, in the light of discussion made herein above, after applying the development cut @
10% to the value of the land, relying upon 4 of 5 RFA-3949-1998 (O&M) alongwith other connected cases --5-- sale instance Ex.P2 coming out to be Rs.2,53,968/- per acre, the market price of the acquired land is thus computed @ Rs.2,28,571/- per acre.
In addition, the landowners shall also be entitled for all other statutory benefits and interest as provided under the 1894 Act (Amended upto-date).
12. In view of the aforesaid discussion, the appeals filed at the instance of landowners are partly allowed, whereas, the cross-appeals filed at the instance of State are hereby dismissed.

13. Further, in case of unfortunate demise of any of the appellants- landowners, if the legal heir(s)-legal representative(s) have not been brought on record, they shall be entitled for filing exemption applications in their own names being legal heirs or legal representatives of the deceased- landowners; subject of course to any testamentary document created by the deceased.
14. Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.

08.10.2025 (HARKESH MANUJA)
sonika JUDGE
